routes.question: Does exhaustive canonical enumeration prove every 11-vertex tournament has a 15-packing?
premises: gentourng emits one representative per isomorphism class
the exact target search is sound
routes.method: canonical generation, independent exact bit-mask packing, fail-only logs, class-count and stream digests
routes.next_test: none; retain the canonical-generation contract as an explicit trusted-base item

routes.question: Is there an 11-vertex tournament whose exact maximum packing is at most 14?
premises: all orientations are represented by 55-bit strings
routes.method: structured cyclic blow-ups, random and score-extreme tournaments, then exhaustive counterexample scan
routes.failure_reason: Every one of the 903753248 canonical representatives has a target-15 Builder witness; no below-target literal was emitted.
routes.next_test: independent full Certifier replay is retained as adversarial audit, not as discovery

routes.question: What exact finite hypergraph problem is equivalent to TT3 packing?
premises: a tournament has one arc on every unordered vertex pair
routes.method: map each transitive vertex triple to a 3-subset of the C(n,2) pair indices; packing becomes 3-set matching
routes.next_test: use relabeling invariance to justify canonical representatives

routes.question: Can deletion to the certified n=10 case force three additional triples?
routes.method: analyze unused-pair graph of a 12-packing and extension triples through the deleted vertex
routes.failure_reason: A 12-packing extends by three triples through the deleted vertex exactly when its admissible leave graph has a 3-matching; nine leave edges alone do not force such a matching.
routes.next_test: not needed for the finite endpoint once the independent exhaustive certificate passes

routes.question: Can malformed input, an incorrect transitivity test, reused arcs, truncation, or an incomplete slice be falsely accepted?
routes.method: fresh verifier, negative controls, independent evaluator, exact count/digest checks
